summary: Tidal burst of short streams in us-west-2 causing regional GPU starvation; autoscaler stuck failing to scale and noisy-tenant amplification
description:
Issue summary:
A customer (EchoMail, dedicated pool in us-west-2) reported a sharp throughput collapse and p99 latency spike beginning ~2026-03-13T09:20 UTC. Symptoms include rapid GPU attach failures, high allocator queue length, and autoscaler failing to add capacity (scale stuck). Pattern: a tidal wave of many short-lived streams from multiple tenants caused slot fragmentation and amplifier effect from a noisy tenant using many tiny streaming connections.

Impact:
- EchoMail: observed ~70% throughput drop for batched routes and p99 latency increase from 120ms to 3.2s on chat generation.
- Other tenants in same dedicated cluster: intermittent timeouts and elevated p95/p99.
- Operational: alert storm for attach_lag and allocator_backpressure in us-west-2.

Environment:
- Deployment: dedicated reserved pool (cluster: dp-west-42) in us-west-2
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.23.0, allocator v0.9.5, autoscaler v2.18.1
- Networking: standard VPC (no customer-side VPN changes reported)

Steps to reproduce (observed reproduction pattern):
1) High-fanout traffic pattern with many short streams (<= 3s) arriving concurrently, mostly from a single tenant cohort.
2) Each short stream requests warmup/prefetch; allocator issues many small allocations and NVLink/KV-cache warmups.
3) Slot fragmentation prevents coalescing into efficient batches; GPU memory pressure grows and thin-slicing increases attach latency.
4) Autoscaler sees transient attach latency and oscillating metrics and enters a cooldown state instead of provisioning, leaving cluster below target capacity.

Observed metrics and logs (selected):
- allocator.attach_latency.p95 (us-west-2): baseline 80ms -> spike 1.8s at 2026-03-13T09:23 UTC
- allocator.queue_depth: 5 -> sustained 230 during burst window
- GPU utilization: uneven across hosts; several nodes at 98% while others idle (slot hoarding pattern)
- autoscaler.log: repeated "scale suppressed: cooldown_policy" messages from 09:24:00 -> 09:40:00
- serving-runtime stderr: repeated kernel queue rejects with "KV cache cold start" during fanout

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support temporarily applied tenant-level rate-limit (throttle) at the gateway for the noisy tenant cohort at 09:45 UTC which immediately reduced short-stream arrival rate by ~85% and allowed allocator queue to drain.
- Manually increased autoscaler max burst limit for the cluster (temporary override) at 09:52 UTC which allowed 2 additional GPU nodes to be provisioned and restore aggregate throughput to ~85% of baseline.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Noisy-tenant with many short streams causes repeated prefetch/kernel warmups, creating NVLink/KV-cache thrash and preventing efficient batching. Evidence: high rate of small allocate/release cycles in allocator logs keyed to tenant id T-echo-308.
- Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler heuristics are overly conservative for very high-frequency short-stream workloads and enter cooldown due to perceived instability. Evidence: autoscaler metrics show multiple scale decisions suppressed during the peak window; scale recommendation was positive but suppressed by cooldown.
- Hypothesis 3: Slot fragmentation and affinity mismatch between multiplexed short streams leads to some GPUs being "hot" while others remain underused. Evidence: host-level GPU utilization skew and logs showing connection affinity stuck to a subset of nodes.

Next steps / action items:
- Short term (SRE + Support): keep tenant-level throttle in place for noisy cohort and monitor for 24 hours. (Owner: Support)
- Mid term (Infra): deploy a targeted autoscaler tweak to relax cooldown sensitivity for clusters experiencing sustained attach_latency (experiment rollout in staging first). (Owner: Mateo Ruiz)
- Mid term (Runtime): add a diagnostic histogram for per-tenant short-stream rate and slot fragmentation to help automated routing decisions. (Owner: Runtime team)
- Long term (Product + Solutions): work with EchoMail to introduce client-side batching or aggregated keepalive to reduce connection churn. (Owner: Solutions)

Notes: customer was kept updated during triage and accepted the temporary throttle as acceptable under dedicated SLA.
